data.reasoning: The disagreement is solely due to an API error in the qwen model, which failed to process the .desktop and .sh files. The deepseek model successfully reviewed all files, including the launcher script and desktop entry, finding them to be standard and safe. The PKGBUILD follows standard AUR practices, fetching from the official upstream GitHub repository with pinned checksums.
data.disagreement_analysis: The qwen model encountered HTTP 400 errors when auditing proton-mail.desktop and proton-mail.sh, resulting in an inconclusive verdict. The deepseek model successfully audited these files and found no issues. There is no actual security disagreement between the models' assessments of the code.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to review proton-mail.desktop and proton-mail.sh due to LLM API errors (HTTP 400).
learnings: The orchestration layer should distinguish between 'inconclusive due to security ambiguity' and 'inconclusive due to tool/API failure'. A tool error on trivial files should not force an overall inconclusive verdict if the failure is clearly a transient API issue.
Implement automatic retries or fallback models for transient API errors (like HTTP 400) during file-level audits to prevent coverage gaps and unnecessary escalations.
